headline: Nvidia had its best day since April 2025 at +8.74% and dragged four indices green - but info tech was the ONLY positive S&P sector, decliners beat advancers on the NYSE, and overnight every OTHER beat-and-raise was SOLD: Marvell -8% after raising two years of guidance. VXN closed at a seven-month low hours before Warsh speaks at 10:00
client_frame_short:
The question this morning: "Nvidia just had its best day in sixteen months, so why do futures point lower?" Because one stock is not a market. Technology was the ONLY S&P sector to finish green yesterday, and more NYSE stocks fell than rose. Overnight, every other company that beat expectations AND raised its forecast was sold anyway - Marvell is down 8% after raising guidance for two straight years. **A tape that punishes good news from everyone except one company is narrow, not strong.**

Nothing here needs a decision from you. Two things are worth knowing. Fed Chair Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole speech at 10:00 this morning, and the options market has priced almost nothing for it - Nasdaq volatility closed at a seven-month low. Meanwhile the odds of a rate HIKE by December sit at 75%, and this week the market moved that hike LATER rather than away.
client_frame:
Start with the number everybody will quote and then with the one they will skip. Nvidia closed at $227.98, up 8.74%, and we checked what that ranks against rather than repeating a wire: on our own daily bars going back two years, the last time the stock gained more in a single session was April 9, 2025. It carried the whole board - the Nasdaq 100 added 1.43%, the Philadelphia semiconductor index 2.33%, the S&P 500 0.72%. Now the number nobody leads with. Information technology was the ONLY S&P sector to close green, and on the New York Stock Exchange more stocks fell than rose. The Dow, which barely owns the AI complex, added 0.20%. So the honest description of Thursday is not a rally; it is one company's earnings report distributed across four index calculations.

The overnight tape then said something clearer, and it is the most useful thing I can hand you this week. Marvell beat and raised guidance for BOTH fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 - and fell 7.95% before the open. Autodesk raised and fell 5.04%. Ulta raised and fell 3.39%. Gap rose 14.1% and Affirm 9.8%, so the market has not stopped rewarding anything, but the pattern across four sessions now is that beating expectations is no longer sufficient and raising guidance is no longer sufficient either. That is what a fully-valued market looks like from the inside: good news gets paid once, at the very top of the leaderboard, and everyone else pays for their multiple. It is also why the semiconductor index still sits 18.8% below its own June record even after yesterday, a fact I would put in front of anyone who thinks the AI trade has only gone up this year.

The second thread is a genuine disagreement between two markets, and when they disagree the disagreement itself is the observation. Equity volatility went to sleep: the VIX settled 14.51, its lowest since August 14, and VXN, the Nasdaq-100 volatility index, settled 20.24, which our own two-year series says is its lowest close since January 22 - a seven-month low. The front-to-three-month VIX ratio steepened to 0.826 from 0.845, which is complacency, not caution. The rate market did the opposite. Thursday's $44 billion 7-year auction stopped at 4.512%, the highest 7-year yield at auction since December 2024, with indirect bidders taking only 60.8% against 70.1% previously - that is soft foreign demand at the highest yield in twenty months. Four Fed officials spoke hawkishly on the same day: Kansas City's Schmid called inflation still stubborn and still sticky, Cleveland's Hammack said now is the time to act, Boston's Collins said it may be appropriate to tighten soon, and Chicago's Goolsbee said everybody should be on edge. And on our own re-derived CME payload the odds of a hike by December are 75.2% while September's odds FELL from 39.6% to 37.6% - the hike moved later in the calendar, it did not go away. I will correct one thing you may read elsewhere this morning: the market is not fully priced for a December hike. It is at three-quarters.

Two dates and a caution. At 10:00 this morning Chair Warsh gives his first Jackson Hole address, and the same minute brings the BLS preliminary payroll benchmark revision - the number that was revised down by 911,000 jobs last year and reset the entire labour-market debate. With July payrolls already at minus 23,000, that release is the strongest potential argument against the hawks, and almost nobody is watching it. BofA's Mark Cabana frames the speech risk usefully: a structural rather than cyclical speech would read dovish and could push the 30-year toward 5.5%. Then a week from today, August payrolls. Outside the US, the disinflation story is getting harder rather than easier - French inflation rose to 2.7% and Spanish to 4.5%, both accelerating, and Tokyo core CPI came in at 1.8% against 1.7% expected with the Bank of Japan now expected to hike as soon as September. Oil fell more than 5% on the week, its first weekly decline in three, but Qatar's mediation in Tehran produced no reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. For clients: the useful frame today is not whether Nvidia was good - it was - but that a market where only one sector rises and every other good result gets sold is a market with no margin for error priced into it, which is precisely when position sizing and a written plan earn their keep.

single_name_moves.note: The single most instructive move of the night and the direct read-through to yesterday's Nvidia euphoria. Marvell beat AND raised guidance for BOTH fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 - and fell 7.95% pre-market. It closed the regular session at $241.45, -1.49%, on our own Polygon bars, and is already 23.7% below its 6/4/26 record close of 316.43. Custom AI silicon and optical interconnect, 24 hours after the largest AI winner printed 106% revenue growth, punished for a raise. If you need one fact to explain why futures are lower after an 8.74% day in Nvidia, this is it

$227.98, +8.74%, and we verified the superlative from our own 501-bar daily series rather than repeating it: the last session with a larger single-day gain was April 9, 2025, at +18.72%. So this is the best day in sixteen months. Two counterweights held in the same window. It is still NOT a record - 3.29% below the 5/14/26 record close of 235.74, so the best day in sixteen months did not even reclaim a high set three months ago. And the index it dominates, the SOX, remains 18.8% below its own June record
Autodesk raised guidance and fell 5.04%. The second of three raise-and-sold names overnight. Reports Tuesday-adjacent peers into the same tape

Ulta Beauty raised guidance and fell 3.39% - the third consecutive raise punished, and this one is a discretionary-consumer read rather than a technology multiple story, which makes the pattern harder to dismiss as an AI-valuation artefact

The exception that keeps the pattern honest: Gap rose 14.1% and Affirm 9.8%. The market has not stopped paying for good news; it has stopped paying for merely-good news from expensive companies. Reporting these alongside the three punished raises is the difference between an observation and a narrative

geo_headlines: THE RALLY WAS ONE STOCK WIDE AND THE BREADTH DATA SAYS SO PLAINLY: Nvidia closed $227.98, +8.74%, and on our own two-year daily series the last larger single-session gain was April 9, 2025 - the best day in sixteen months. It lifted the Nasdaq 100 1.43%, the SOX 2.33% and the S&P 500 0.72% to its highest close since 8/17. But information technology at +3.4% was the ONLY positive S&P sector, decliners beat advancers 1.02 to 1 on the NYSE, and the Dow managed +0.20%. Nvidia is still 3.29% below its own 5/14/26 record close of 235.74 and the semiconductor index remains 18.808% below its 6/22/26 record close of 14634.72. Every one of those figures is re-derived from our own bars this run, not taken from a wire. Nasdaq futures were about -0.3% pre-open.

EVERY OTHER BEAT-AND-RAISE OVERNIGHT WAS SOLD, AND THAT IS THE TRADEABLE PATTERN RATHER THAN THE NVIDIA PRINT: Marvell beat and raised guidance for BOTH fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 and fell 7.95% pre-market; Autodesk raised and fell 5.04%; Ulta raised and fell 3.39%. Gap +14.1% and Affirm +9.8% were the exceptions, so this is not a market that has stopped rewarding results - it is a market that has stopped rewarding merely-good results from richly-valued companies. This is now the fourth consecutive session of the same pattern. Marvell is the sharpest case because it is the closest comparable to Nvidia in the AI silicon chain: same demand story, same customers, opposite reaction, 24 hours apart.

THE VOLATILITY MARKET FELL ASLEEP HOURS BEFORE A FED CHAIR KEYNOTE AND THE BOND MARKET DID NOT: VXN, the Nasdaq-100 volatility index, settled 20.24, -5.51%, its LOWEST CLOSE SINCE 2026-01-22 - a seven-month low computed over our own two-year series, not reported from a wire. The VIX settled 14.51, -4.60%, lowest since 8/14, and VIX3M settled 17.56, putting front-to-three-month at 0.826 versus 0.845 on Wednesday: STEEPER contango, which is complacency and not caution. Against that, Thursday's $44B 7-year auction stopped at 4.512%, the highest 7-year auction stop since December 2024, with a 2.50 bid-to-cover and indirects taking just 60.8% against 70.1% prior. Equity vol says nothing will happen at 10:00; the auction says real money is demanding materially more yield to fund the government at seven years. When two markets disagree this cleanly, the DIVERGENCE is the observation.

THE SEPTEMBER HIKE DID NOT DISAPPEAR THIS WEEK, IT MOVED LATER - AND WE ARE CORRECTING A WIRE PARAPHRASE ON THIS: our CME cohort refreshed to Thursday's settle and the move was NOT uniform. Cumulative hike odds FELL at the near meetings and ROSE at the far ones: September 39.6% to 37.6%, October 54.3% to 52.8%, December 73.5% to 75.2%, January 2027 78.2% to 80.3% - every field verified against yesterday's raw payload rather than against a summary. December carries a 29.84% chance of TWO OR MORE hikes and cut probability is still exactly ZERO at every meeting through January 2027. A wire account this morning described the market as fully priced for a December hike; our own primary payload says 75.2%, which is not the same claim and is the one we ship. Four Fed speakers pushed hawkish Thursday: Schmid (still stubborn and still sticky), Hammack (now is the time to act), Collins (appropriate to tighten policy soon) and Goolsbee (everybody should be on edge).

THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL RELEASE TODAY IS NOT THE SPEECH, AND ALMOST NOBODY IS WATCHING IT: at 10:00 AM ET, the same minute Chair Warsh begins, the BLS publishes its PRELIMINARY PAYROLL BENCHMARK REVISION for March 2026 plus QCEW Q1 - confirmed on the BLS's own schedule. Last year's preliminary benchmark revision was a DOWNWARD revision of 911,000 jobs and it reset the entire labour-market debate for months. July payrolls were already MINUS 23,000 with unemployment at 4.1%. A large downward revision would be the single strongest argument against the four hawks who spoke yesterday, and it lands buried under a keynote. Note precisely what it does and does not do: monthly CES estimates are NOT revised today - the benchmark is applied with the January reference period in February. Michigan FINAL August sentiment lands at the same minute too, with the preliminary at 51.0 against a July final of 55.2.

WARSH SPEAKS AT 10:00 AND EVEN THE TITLE OF THE SLOT IS DISPUTED BETWEEN TWO PRIMARY SOURCES: the Kansas City Fed's own program titles it Opening Remarks, the Federal Reserve Board's August calendar says Keynote Remarks - both primary, conflict noted and NOT reconciled. 8:00 a.m. Mountain, chaired by Kristin Forbes of MIT, streamed on youtube.com/kansascityfed, and only the Chair's address is streamed. Theme: Financial Innovation, Implications for Payments and Policy. BofA's Mark Cabana gives the cleanest stated risk: a structural rather than cyclical speech would read dovish and could push the 30Y above 5.5%. REFUTED for the record: a Bowman 12:45 PM slot circulating this morning does not exist - that Board-calendar row's date column reads 8, not 28, and Warsh is the ONLY Fed speaker today. Later Friday sessions: Prasad and Mann 10:30 ET, Duffie and Schnabel 11:55, a BIS-OECD-IMF panel with Hernandez de Cos, Scarpetta and Georgieva 12:55, Rogoff at the 3:00 PM luncheon.

EUROPEAN AND JAPANESE INFLATION BOTH ACCELERATED OVERNIGHT, WHICH MAKES THIS A GLOBAL TIGHTENING STORY RATHER THAN AN AMERICAN ONE: French harmonised inflation rose to 2.7% from 2.4% and Spanish to 4.5% from 3.9%, both accelerating and both strengthening the ECB hike case, with the German flash due Monday 8/31. Tokyo core CPI printed +1.8% year over year against 1.7% expected with core-core at 2.0%, and the Bank of Japan is now expected to hike as soon as its September 17-18 meeting. Bunds 3.26%, +1bp; gilts 5.05%, +2bp. Equity markets ignored all of it: STOXX 600 655.64, +0.6% at 07:08 GMT, DAX 26,516.82, +0.61%, CAC about +1%, FTSE roughly flat near 10,792. Three Asian indices - Nikkei, Hang Seng and Shanghai - are OMITTED from our data rows this morning because sources conflict, two of them on the SIGN.

TWO OPEN GEOPOLITICAL TAILS THAT HAVE NOT RESOLVED, BOTH DATED: Qatar's Prime Minister was in Tehran on Thursday and there was NO reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's stated preconditions are an end to the blockade, compensation and sanctions relief; an Iran-Oman corridor was agreed in principle only. A tanker was struck by a projectile in Hormuz on Thursday, five ships transited on Aug 25 against seven previously, and the IMO counts 70 incidents and 19 seafarers killed since Feb 28 - yet crude fell more than 5% on the week, its first weekly decline in three. Separately, Treasury Secretary Bessent's promised designation of a large foreign financial institution is STILL NOT SOURCED: no Treasury release appeared on Aug 27 or 28, which makes it live headline risk today rather than a settled fact. And a dated one to diarise: Canada's counter-tariffs take effect 12:01 AM ET on Sept 8, roughly US$20B at 15, 25 and 50% rates, with the item list CUT from 874 to 629 on Aug 26.
